name: MIC5219-3.3YM5-TR
title: 500 mA peak output low-dropout regulator, fixed and adjustable, with enable
summary: The MIC5219 is a low-dropout linear regulator built to supply 500 mA peaks, such as start-up inrush, while running 150 mA to 200 mA continuously; continuous current is bounded only by package dissipation. Dropout is about 10 mV at light load and 500 mV maximum at 500 mA, output accuracy is ±1 % at 25 °C, and a BYP capacitor gives ultra-low-noise operation. It runs from 2.5 V to 12 V, has an enable input with near-zero shutdown current, current limit, thermal shutdown and reversed-battery protection, and comes in SOT23-5, MSOP-8, 2 mm × 2 mm VDFN-6 and TDFN-6 with fixed outputs from 2.5 V to 5.0 V or an adjustable output. MIC5219-3.3YM5-TR is the 3.3 V SOT23-5 part, marked LG33, on reels of 3,000.

rows: IOUT = 100 µA to 500 mA, Note 2, –40°C ≤ TJ ≤ +125°C

notes: Rows whose conditions carry –40°C ≤ TJ ≤ +125°C hold over that junction range; the rest are at TJ = +25°C. Four single cells also hold over the full range: the 40 ppm/°C temperature coefficient, the 8 µA maximum quiescent current at VEN ≤ 0.18V, the 1000 mA maximum current limit and the 0.05 %/W thermal regulation figure.
Note 1: the temperature coefficient is the largest output change seen across the temperature range, divided by the width of that range.

Note 2: regulation is tested with short pulses at a low duty cycle, so the junction temperature does not move; load regulation is tested from 100 µA up to 500 mA. Output drift caused by self-heating is counted under thermal regulation instead.
Note 3: dropout is the input-to-output difference at which the output has sagged 2 % below the value it holds with 1 V of headroom.
Note 4: ground pin current is the regulator's quiescent current plus the base current of its pass transistor; the supply delivers the load current plus this current.
Note 5: VEN is the voltage applied from outside to the EN pin.
Note 6: thermal regulation is the output change a time t after a step in dissipation, leaving out line and load regulation; the figure is for a 500 mA step of load with VIN = 12V, read at t = 10 ms.
Note 7: CBYP is an optional capacitor on the BYP pin, or on the ADJ pin of adjustable versions.
Misprint: the thermal regulation row should refer to Note 6, not Note 3.
Misprint: the 2.0 V minimum is the enable logic-high level (VENH), not a logic-low figure.

circuits.title: 5 V ultra-low-noise regulator
circuits.description: A 5 V fixed part in MSOP-8 run from 6 V. A 2.2 µF tantalum capacitor on OUT keeps the loop stable and 470 pF on BYP quiets the reference for lowest noise. EN is brought out as an enable/shutdown logic line, and the four GND pins are tied together to ground.

circuits.title: 3.3 V ultra-low-noise regulator
circuits.description: The 3.3 V SOT23-5 part fed from 4 V. The output carries a 2.2 µF tantalum capacitor to ground and BYP carries 470 pF to ground. EN is a separate enable/shutdown logic input.

circuits.title: Ultra-low-noise regulator, fixed output, VDFN
circuits.description: A fixed-voltage VDFN part between VIN and VOUT with COUT on the output. CBYP from BYP to ground is optional and lowers noise. EN is driven as an enable/shutdown logic line; pin 5 is left open.
notes: COUT is at least 1 µF without CBYP and at least 2.2 µF with CBYP = 470 pF.

circuits.title: Ultra-low-noise regulator, adjustable output, TDFN
circuits.description: The adjustable TDFN part. R1 from OUT to ADJ and R2 from ADJ to ground set the output voltage, a 2.2 µF polarised capacitor sits on OUT, and 470 pF from ADJ to ground lowers noise. EN is an enable/shutdown logic input; pin 6 is left open.

circuits.title: Low-noise fixed-voltage regulator
circuits.description: The basic fixed-output circuit: EN is tied to IN so the regulator is always on, BYP is left open and a 1 µF capacitor on OUT is the minimum for stability.

circuits.title: Ultra-low-noise fixed-voltage regulator
circuits.description: The fixed-output circuit with 470 pF added between BYP and ground for lower noise. Because the bypass capacitor is fitted, the output capacitor rises to 2.2 µF. EN is tied to IN.

circuits.title: Low-noise adjustable regulator
circuits.description: The adjustable part with EN tied to IN. R1 from OUT to ADJ and R2 from ADJ to ground set the output, and a 1 µF polarised capacitor sits on OUT.

operation.text: The part is aimed at loads of 150 mA to 200 mA that need a short 500 mA burst at start-up. In SOT23-5 or MSOP-8 it delivers 500 mA of start-up current; continuous current is limited only by package dissipation and layout, and with enough heat sinking and headroom 500 mA can be held continuously.

Driving EN above 2 V turns the regulator on; EN accepts CMOS logic levels. Low or open, EN shuts the regulator down and supply current falls nearly to zero. Where shutdown is not used, EN is tied to IN.
Fit 1 µF from IN to GND when the input runs more than 10 inches of wire from the AC filter capacitor, or when the input is a battery.

OUT needs a capacitor to GND or the regulator oscillates. Minimum: 1 µF without CBYP, 2.2 µF with CBYP = 470 pF; outputs below 3 V take at least 22 µF to hold down overshoot at turn-on. More capacitance gives better transient response, with no upper limit. ESR should be about 1 Ω or less, with a resonant frequency above 1 MHz; capacitors with very low ESR can cause oscillation or poorly damped transients. Most tantalum and aluminium electrolytic capacitors work and film capacitors also work at higher cost. Many aluminium electrolytes freeze near –30°C, so solid tantalum is the choice below –25°C. At light load less capacitance is needed: 0.47 µF below 10 mA, 0.33 µF below 1 mA.
With no load beyond its own internal divider the regulator stays stable and in regulation, which suits CMOS RAM keep-alive supplies.

BYP is the internal reference node. 470 pF from BYP to GND filters the reference and cuts output noise markedly. CBYP lowers the phase margin, so with it the output capacitor is normally 2.2 µF or more. Start-up time grows with CBYP: a larger value gives a slower output ramp, and leaving CBYP off gives the fastest turn-on.
Although ADJ draws little current, best results need R2 of 470 kΩ or less. Adding 470 pF between ADJ and GND lowers output noise.
The part has current limiting, thermal shutdown and reversed-battery protection. Short-circuit current is 700 mA typical, 1000 mA maximum, at VOUT = 0 V.

The die is limited to TJ(MAX) = +125°C, and θJA depends on the layout: in SOT23-5 220°C/W on the minimum footprint and 170°C/W with 1 square inch of 2 oz copper; in MSOP-8 160°C/W and 70°C/W. Ground planes in multilayer boards, wide traces at the pads and large supply buses all improve heat flow.

Pulsing the load with EN lowers average dissipation, letting the part run from a higher input voltage when high current is needed only in bursts. The safe-operating-region graphs give, for SOT23-5 and MSOP-8 on a minimum footprint and on 1 square inch of copper at 25°C, 50°C and 85°C ambient, the largest input-to-output drop allowed at each duty cycle for loads of 100 mA to 500 mA; the lower the temperature, the larger the region. For a steady load with occasional peaks, the dissipation of each part of the cycle is weighted by its duty cycle and the two are added.
